public_rationale: The first part holds. After GPT-5 launched, many ChatGPT users demanded GPT-4o back, and OpenAI restored it for paying users within days (e1). The second part, 'almost nobody felt satisfied', overstates things. In the same week, CNBC reported that Cursor, Vercel and Factory made GPT-5 their default model, and Box's CEO called it 'unbelievably well' performing (e2, e3). A contemporaneous report described users as split, not uniformly unhappy (e4). Consumer backlash was real, but satisfaction was not rare among developer and enterprise customers.
limitations: No representative survey exists, so the balance of satisfied and dissatisfied users is inferred from reporting.
Enterprise praise came partly from OpenAI launch partners, who may have had reasons to be positive.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Almost no one was satisfied with GPT-5, and some customers wanted the old models back.

statement.excerpt: Some customers even wanted the old models back. Almost nobody felt satisfied.

from_speaker: Some customers even wanted the old models back
our_interpretation: The claim covers reactions to GPT-5 in the week between its launch (2025-08-07) and the post (2025-08-14).
Part A, 'some customers wanted the old models back', holds if users publicly asked for GPT-4o or other legacy models and OpenAI responded.

Part B, 'almost nobody felt satisfied', is read plainly as satisfaction with GPT-5 being rare across its users. Clear reports of substantial satisfied user groups, such as enterprise or developer customers, would contradict it.
criteria.support_condition: Reports show users demanding the old models back, and reports show dissatisfaction was near-universal, with few satisfied users.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reports show that no meaningful group asked for the old models, or that substantial groups of users and customers were satisfied with GPT-5 in its launch week.
